content: Amphotec (amphotericin B cholesteryl sulfate) is a medication used for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis in patients who cannot tolerate amphotericin B deoxycholate (conventional formulation) due to renal impairment or unacceptable toxicity, or in cases where prior therapy with amphotericin B deoxycholate has failed. The recommended dosage for adults is 3-4 mg/kg administered intravenously once daily. The initial infusion rate is 1 mg/kg/hour, and subsequent infusions may be shortened to a 2-hour duration if the patient tolerates the treatment well. Adverse effects associated with Amphotec include chills (50-77%), fever (33-55%), hypokalemia (7-26%), elevated serum creatinine (12-21%), hyperbilirubinemia (2-19%), hypotension (9-12%), tachycardia (9-12%), nausea (8-12%), vomiting (6-11%), abnormal liver function tests (4-11%), hypertension (7-9%), hypoxia (5-9%), dyspnea (4-9%), headache (4-8%), hypomagnesemia (4-7%), increased alkaline phosphatase (3-7%), thrombocytopenia (1-7%), hyperglycemia (1-6%), and hypersensitivity reactions. This medication is indicated for patients with progressive and potentially fatal fungal infections. It is not recommended for noninvasive fungal infections, such as oral thrush, vaginal candidiasis, or esophageal candidiasis, in patients with normal neutrophil counts. Caution is advised when co-administering Amphotec with other drugs that may cause hypokalemia (e.g., corticosteroids, digoxin) or nephrotoxic medications. Amphotec is classified as Pregnancy Category B, meaning that controlled studies in pregnant women have not shown evidence of fetal risk. It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in breast milk, so caution is advised during lactation. To prepare the medication, gently shake the vial by hand and rotate it until all solids are dissolved. The resulting fluid may appear opalescent or clear. Do not filter the solution or use an in-line filter. Use a separate infusion line for administration; if an existing IV line is used, flush it with 5% dextrose (D5W) before infusion. The initial infusion rate is 1 mg/kg/hour, and subsequent infusions may be shortened to 2 hours if tolerated. Unopened vials should be stored at room temperature, protected from light and excessive heat. After reconstitution, the drug should be refrigerated at 2-8°C (36-46°F) and used within 24 hours. After further dilution with 5% dextrose, the solution should also be refrigerated and used within 24 hours. Do not freeze the medication, and discard any partially used vials. This information is provided for general educational purposes. Formulary status and recommendations may vary, so it is important to consult the applicable plan provider for the most current information.
